name: Firearm Business Register and Inspection Pack (dealers, gunsmiths, ranges, security-firm armouries)
buyer: Licensed firearm dealers, gunsmiths, shooting ranges, and PSIRA-registered security companies holding business firearms
trigger: Firearms Control Act 60 of 2000 (s39(6), Regulations 38-40) dealer registers, SAP 350 stock returns and an annual stock register to the Central Firearms Registrar; SAPS compliance inspections (3,728 reported Feb 2026; s120(1) offences)
evidence: https://www.sanews.gov.za/node/79677 (3,728 inspections of dealers and security companies, 18 Feb 2026); https://pretorianews.co.za/news/2026-03-20-calvin-mathibelis-security-firm-under-scrutiny-for-incomplete-firearms-records/ (Durban security firm register discrepancies, Mar 2026); https://www.protectionweb.co.za/civil-security/saps-detail-progress-and-partnerships-in-new-firearms-management-system/ (FCMS still in development, Gauteng pilot, no go-live date, no third-party interface mentioned); https://pmg.org.za/files/1/firearmsbill_SAAADA.htm and https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2023-07-13-sas-gun-controls-dire-dealers-association-speaks-out (the electronic dealer link was never built)
existing: No local product found for dealer or security-firm registers. Foreign armoury systems exist (Armorymaster by Traceability Solutions, ArmorerLink) and consumer firearm-log apps, none tied to SAPS formats. Competitor search done (one search): nothing local found.
unchecked: Number of licensed dealers, gunsmiths, ranges and security firms with business firearms; the exact mandatory register formats and retention rules; whether a local dealer POS already has a firearm register module; whether FCMS will give dealers a portal that makes this redundant; willingness to pay; sector concerns about uploading sensitive stock data.

first_check.duty: Firearms Control Act 60 of 2000 and the Firearms Control Regulations, Regulation 37 (dealer registers). Dealers must keep a Firearms Stock Register, an Ammunition Stock Register, a Firearms Safe Custody Register and a staff register, filled in at each receipt and disposal. Registers may be paper books, with every page signed and stamped by the Designated Firearms Officer (DFO) before use, or computer printouts handed to the DFO within 7 days after each month end for signing and stamping. Records are kept for 10 years at the licensed premises. Ammunition returns are due only when the Registrar directs by written notice. The page index lists a separate weekly-returns regulation (Reg 39), but I did not read its text. Breaches are offences under s120(1). SAPS reported 3,728 compliance inspections of gun dealers and security companies (SAnews, 18 Feb 2026), which led to a dealer arrest and the seizure of 537 firearms. The claim cites s39(6), Regulations 38-40 and the 'SAP 350' form; I did not verify those citations. The register rule I confirmed is Reg 37. Security-company armouries also keep registers, and their staff need monthly Regulation 21 training (from job ads; I did not read the regulation itself).
first_check.market: I found no current count of licensed dealers, gunsmiths or ranges. For security firms, PSIRA reported 10,830 active registered security businesses (2023/24 briefing). PSIRA targeted about 1,425 firearm inspections of security businesses (2019/20 plan), and a 2013/14 analysis found 313 security businesses using firearms. The firearm-holding subset is probably in the low thousands at most. The 3,728 SAPS inspections give a rough upper bound for dealers plus security firms combined. Overall the market is small: probably about 1,000 to 4,000 businesses (my rough estimate).
first_check.competitor: I found no South African dealer or security-firm register software. Point-of-sale systems listed on Capterra South Africa (Rapid Gun Systems, AXIS POS, AIM POS, Windward) are built for US ATF/FFL rules. Armoury systems (Systematics ARMS, ArmorerLink, Cloud Weapons Express, Traceability Solutions) are foreign or aimed at law enforcement. CybateSoft (South Africa) does weapon marking and track-and-trace, but its listing does not mention SAPS register formats. The state Firearms Control Management System (FCMS) is still rolling out in phases. Its Release 02 was pushed to the end of January 2026, and a pilot is planned at three Gauteng police stations. I found no go-live date and no dealer portal. Dealers and gunsmiths do sit on a Technical Work Team for FCMS, so a future state dealer interface remains a risk. I did not check for a locally built dealer point-of-sale system with a register module or with in-house spreadsheets, beyond these searches.
first_check.reason: The duty is real and enforced. Regulation 37 of the Firearms Control Regulations requires dealers to keep firearm stock, ammunition stock, safe-custody and staff registers for 10 years. If a dealer keeps them on computer, it must hand printouts to the Designated Firearms Officer within 7 days of each month end for signing and stamping, so the work recurs every month. SAPS reported 3,728 inspections of dealers and security firms in February 2026, and breaches are offences under s120(1). I found no South African software for these registers. Available tools are US ATF/FFL point-of-sale systems or generic armoury systems. Weaknesses: the market is small and could not be counted, buyers are wary of sharing sensitive data, paper books remain legal, and a dealer channel in FCMS could make the product redundant.

challenge_check.killer: No outright killer found. Main risk: the SAPS FCMS is designed to take dealers' returns electronically, and a Technical Work Team of dealer, gunsmith and manufacturer associations is involved in building it. Release 02 was due by the end of January 2026; I could not verify whether it went live.
challenge_check.reason: I found no South African dealer or security-firm register product. The products that turned up are foreign: US FFL point-of-sale systems, plus armoury and law-enforcement tools such as Cloud Weapons Express and NextGen IoT. The regulations allow registers to be kept as computer printouts, so software could do the job. Two things pull the score down. First, the state's FCMS is designed to let licensed dealers submit their returns electronically (Cape Times, Nov 2024). It is late and its status in 2026 is unverified, but it could cover the return-filing part. Second, the dealer market is small: about 600 licences held by about 300 companies (an old SAAADA figure), and one report says only about 50 dealers remained by 2006. 16,704 security firms are registered with PSIRA, but I found no count of how many hold firearms. The large guarding firms already employ armourers.
